title: The Swiss leaf-out delay per 1,000 m of elevation decreased within fixed stations in 1960-2016 but did not decrease further in 2017-2025; winter warmth explained under one third
abstract: Question: Vitasse et al. (2018) reported that the leaf-out delay with elevation (EPS) in Switzerland decreased from 34 to 22 days per 1,000 m in 1960-2016, mainly because winters became warmer. Is the decrease a station-network effect, did it continue in 2017-2025, does it repeat in Germany, and how much does winter warmth explain? Data: MeteoSwiss phenology records for beech, hazel, larch and spruce (393 station-species series, 19,815 records), DWD records for beech, larch and spruce in Germany (3,667 series, 157,610 records), MeteoSwiss NBCN and DWD monthly temperatures. Method: Vitasse station rules from 1960-2016 data only; yearly elevation slopes; station fixed-effects panels with two-way clustered errors; seven predictions fitted on 1960-2016 and tested on 2017-2025. Results: The Swiss trend line went from 33.1 to 23.7 days per 1,000 m (1960-2016). The within-station decrease was -1.84 days per 1,000 m per decade (95% CI -2.7 to -1.0), so network change does not cause it. In 2017-2025 the Swiss mean EPS was 25.3, near the 2007-2016 mean of 24.2 and above the trend prediction of 22.9; the within-station departure from the trend was +3.0 (95% CI -0.8 to +6.8). In Germany the decrease was smaller (-0.73 per decade, 95% CI -1.57 to +0.11), and the 2017-2025 EPS (22.1) equalled the 2007-2016 mean (22.3). The 2007-2016 mean predicted 2017-2025 better than the trend in both countries. Warm November-January periods went with a smaller EPS in both periods (Swiss slope -1.42 days per 1,000 m per C in 1960-2016, -1.39 in 2017-2025), but winter warming explained only 5-29% of the long decrease, depending on the model and country. Limitations: nine test years gave only 5-7% power to separate a continued decrease from a stop, so the result is no clear continuation, not a proven stop. Observer changes inside stations, the narrow German elevation range and regional temperature indices limit inference. Record-level source data are not bundled; scripts download them.

Black line: 1960-2016 trend and its extrapolation (dashed). Dotted line: 2007-2016 mean. Coloured bars: within-station period estimates (station fixed effects), anchored at the 1960s level, with 95% CIs.

Within-station estimates. A: change of EPS per decade in 1960-2016. B: 2017-2025 EPS minus the extrapolated 1960-2016 trend. Pooled species (large points) and single species. 95% CIs from station and year two-way clustered errors.

citations.reason: We reproduce and test out of sample its 1960-2016 decrease of the elevation-induced leaf-out shift and its winter-temperature explanation.
Related campaign test of a change in leaf-out temperature sensitivity in the same German and Swiss networks; it also found that a reported decrease did not continue.
Shows that station membership changes can shift Swiss leaf-out trends; we use station fixed effects for this reason.
Related campaign study of Swiss cherry bloom elevation slopes and spring temperature contrasts.
